text: {"score":4,"justification":"The summary is accurate against the card and cautious. 19% of 837 claims were 99215 against 2.1% expected, risk-adjusted score 12.51, z 2.73, and 57.9% of 99215 on patients with 0-1 conditions are all correct. Documentation figures match: 17 records, 4 documented 99215 with 2 below billed (50%), and 5 of 12 documented 99214/99215 below billed. The unmatched '42' is a legitimate ratio (5/12 = 41.7%). Cited claims support their sentences, and the wording 'not a finding' is appropriately hedged. Next steps are concrete, naming claims for chart requests and coder re-scoring. Weaknesses: the headline pools 99214 with 99215, and the 99215-specific rate is the more relevant one. The example low-complexity claims are generic and not the strongest; C0326287, an asthma visit, is weak. Next steps request charts for only three claims, and C0326287 has no documentation returned. Next steps ask for an audit trail even though the summary says none was received, which is not clearly distinguished from a new request. The 9% comparison rate is not on the card (the card shows 0.091 for 99215, which does match). The 'problems 24%/late 6%' note-check figures are not verifiable from the card but may come from tool output. Missing-data flags are limited. The summary does not mention that 5 of the 99215 documented claims... only 4 documented, so thin sample size is not flagged.","problems":["Headline pools 99214 and 99215 (5 of 12), which blurs the 99215-focused finding; the 42% figure is a derived ratio and fine, but the pooling is not explained","Only 4 documented 99215 claims; small sample is not flagged as a caveat","Example low-complexity claims chosen are weak (asthma, depression) rather than the most striking cases such as Z09 or back pain visits","Next steps request charts and audit trail for C0326287, which has no returned documentation, and the audit-trail request follows a statement that none was received without clarity","Note-check percentages (problems 24%, late 6%) cannot be verified from the card","Does not note that high-complexity patients also bill 99215 at normal rates or that diagnosis codes like Z09 suggest low complexity"]}
